primaryEvidence.source: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 3, section 9.7 Semiconductor Devices

anchors.supports: Joining doped regions; electron diffusion and recombination; fixed positive donor and negative acceptor ions localized near the interface; depletion-layer field and equilibrium zero net current.
Positive battery terminal on n gives reverse bias, increased barrier and wider depletion layer; positive terminal on p gives forward bias, reduced barrier and narrower depletion layer.
Minority-carrier contribution opposite to forward current, small reverse current in the elementary diode model, and a distinct large-current breakdown regime at sufficiently strong reverse bias.
Nonlinear diode current-voltage behavior; the elementary reverse saturation description is not a law for arbitrary reverse voltage.

attributionLimits: The bulk-neutrality interpretation is an inference from dopant charge compensation and the primary text's localization of excess charge at the junction, not a purported verbatim neutrality statement in this cache.

Carrier versus conventional-current direction also follows the sign of each carrier and the preceding authoritative page's hole-motion explanation; the cache's carrier-flow shorthand is not used to reverse conventional current.
The qualitative status and large forward/reverse disparity of source Figure 226 are explicit in p0274#5. OpenStax's separate figure is not evidence for the pixels or scales of Figure 226.

Rectification and the warning that a unidirectional current need not have constant magnitude are assessed from p0274#6 and the meaning of alternating current; this cache is not falsely cited as a description of a smoothing circuit.

The cache contains a numerical worked example and content about transistors, amplifiers and digital circuits. None is imported into this lesson. Extracted mathematical glyph repetitions and the worked example are not used to supply new equations, quantities or exercises.

titleReview.finding: The Chinese title is unchanged, and the English title accurately identifies current across the junction of the two doping types. Card identity and printed number 111 are retained in the Chinese template.

science: Donor doping on the source-described left gives n-type material with majority electrons; acceptor doping on the right gives p-type material with majority holes. This is a textual source match, not a verification of the figure.

Letters identify conduction type, not macroscopic negative and positive half-samples. This does not deny the local fixed space charge near the junction; the following sentences explain that local charge.
The hole description is an age-level vacancy model, not a claim that a hole is an additional proton or a moving impurity atom.

Electrons and holes diffuse down their respective concentration gradients. Electrons filling holes is a valid introductory description of recombination. Fixed dopant ions remain; recombination is not presented as generating freely mobile ions.

The resulting field opposes further majority-carrier diffusion and creates a potential-energy barrier. At equilibrium, drift and diffusion currents balance; the text correctly says no sustained net current, not that all microscopic motion stops or that all carriers disappear.

science: Battery positive on p and negative on n is correct forward-bias polarity. The operational condition is p at higher potential than n; the following relative-potential sentence prevents the positive/negative wording from being a claim of an absolute potential zero.
Applied forward voltage lowers the junction barrier and narrows the mobile-carrier-depleted region. This is not a claim that every forward voltage removes the entire barrier.

Electrons cross n to p and holes cross p to n by diffusion in the introductory junction model. The battery supplies charge for sustained conduction, so the account does not stop at an isolated recombination transient.

Electron motion is opposite to conventional current and hole motion is with conventional current. Both forward carrier contributions therefore correspond to conventional current from p to n through the junction.

Easy conduction and relatively low resistance are qualitative forward-versus-reverse comparisons in this discussion, not a fixed ohmic resistance, zero resistance, or a universal claim about arbitrarily small applied voltage.

science: Polarity reversal correctly gives p on the negative terminal and n on the positive terminal. Reverse applied voltage increases the barrier and widens the depleted region.

Minority electrons cross p to n; minority holes cross n to p. Applying the preceding conventional-current rule gives reverse conventional current n to p. Neither minority-carrier identity nor direction is swapped.

The small reverse current is explicitly nonzero and attributed mainly to minority carriers, rather than to the much more numerous majority carriers. This is appropriate in the elementary non-breakdown model, not an assertion of ideal zero leakage or of a universal leakage mechanism for every physical device.

The bilingual operating-range phrase has no definition anywhere in the inspected lesson. A reader cannot tell that the small-current/high-resistance comparison excludes reverse breakdown. The primary cache explicitly distinguishes sufficiently strong reverse bias with large current. This unresolved conceptual limit prevents text SCI PASS.

Figures 226a, b and c are explicitly described as qualitative, without precise readable current or voltage values. The source's large forward/reverse disparity is retained; a same-scale or similar-magnitude interpretation is explicitly rejected. No curve, tick, origin glyph or breakdown point is inferred from images.

science: Directional asymmetry and smaller forward than reverse resistance correctly summarize the intended non-breakdown operating account. They are not a constant-resistance or arbitrary-reverse-voltage law; the lesson-wide limit must be defined in block 7.
Rectification is described as strongly restricting reverse current and allowing mainly one current direction, not as a perfect reverse-current cutoff.
The final sentence explicitly distinguishes direction from magnitude: rectified current may vary with time. No smoothing, regulation, constant output, efficiency or waveform value is claimed.

ageAndConceptualLimits.audience: The charter's strong eight-year-old self-learner reading serious secondary-level physics, with preceding electron, hole and doping context.
strengths: More numerous and less numerous carriers are explained before technical majority/minority terminology is used.
The depletion region is described as having few mobile carriers, not no charge of any kind.
The energy-obstacle analogy does not require a numerical threshold, energy band calculation or a statistical derivation.
Zero equilibrium net current is distinguished from a sustained biased current.
Carrier motion, conventional-current direction, voltage magnitude, qualitative graph trends and rectification's nonconstant magnitude are distinguished explicitly.
limitsAssessed: Doping labels do not imply overall charged bulk halves; local junction space charge is compatible with that statement.
Introductory diffusion/recombination/drift balance is not a universal device model at all temperatures, fields and structures.
Relative low/high resistance is a qualitative comparison, not an ohmic linear I-V relation.
The majority/minority explanation and small reverse current require a non-breakdown operating range, presently undefined.
No quantitative current, voltage, resistance, reverse threshold or waveform can be read into source Figure 226.
A rectified current is not necessarily constant, smoothed or regulated.
ageAndConceptualLimits.notClaimed: No child usability trial, renderer layout review or image-based readability verification was performed.

requiredCorrections.problem: The full frozen lesson never defines that operating range. Its same-voltage comparison and high-reverse-resistance conclusion can consequently be read as holding even under strong reverse bias. The primary text distinguishes a breakdown regime with large reverse current.
